precepts.text: Another word for teaching. You going out, and you start with an L. Luke 14:23.
precepts.point: You're teaching for who? Teaching our people. Teaching for the Lord. Okay. Where's that at? We're teaching for our people. Yeah. You close, because you teach. Another word for teaching. You going out, and you start with an L. Luke 14. Starts with an L. It has an A. It has an O. Labour. Okay. So you labouring for who? The Lord. Luke 14:23. Oh, you labour for who? You said before. For our people to wake up. Yeah. Okay. Tell me. You know what I'm talking about, sir? Let me hear.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
“He that hath travelled is full of prudence. When I travelled, I saw many things”. Travelling doing what? Teaching. And another word for teaching, when you are going out, starts with an L: labour. That is Luke 14:23, the servant sent out by his lord. You are labouring for the Lord, for our people to wake up.

Sirach says the same of himself: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” You travel the world and seek out people that want to learn. But first you have to keep the commandments, learn and study, and then go out and teach. Military men travel too; they have been to Syria and Iraq, but they cannot tell you about Dura Europos or the walls of Cyrus. They travel, but they have not studied to know what to look for.

Judith shows why the labour matters: “Now therefore, O brethren, let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us, and the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.” The people are depending on us, so it is our job to study, get right, and travel to share the word with our people. Later somebody comes behind you, and you share your experience and teach them. That is part of how you go from milk to meat.

The labour brings experience you cannot get staying home. In Cuba the police came with nightsticks and a paddy wagon; teaching without a license there could bring two years in jail with no trial, and the police chief said this teaching would cause a revolution. Having gone through that, the brethren learned there is a different way to approach it, not to stop teaching there. That is why it is good to get around learned men who have travelled: they understand more than they can express in one conversation.

And the one who labours for the Lord is kept by him: “I was ofttimes in danger of death: yet I was delivered because of these things.” “Whoso feareth the Lord shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope.” If you are sincere in this truth and really keeping his commandments, that spirit will come on you and you will not fear. They said nobody could go up into Laventille in Trinidad because of the gangs; the brethren went up there to teach, and it put a spirit on those men, and now they go up there.

precepts.text: Go out into the highways and hedges and compel them to come in.
precepts.point: They went throughout all the cities and taught the people, the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.”

That is what Jehoshaphat's princes and Levites did. They “had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.” It is the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters”: hate means be willing to cut them off if they are keeping you from God’s law. “Yea, and his own life also”: we all had goals before we heard this gospel, some of them unlawful that would have made lots of money. Some of us are struggling now, and we think if I had taken the other road I wouldn’t be struggling like this. That’s how Satan plays with you.

points: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, come on, go out quickly into the streets. Go out quickly into the streets. Read. And lanes of the city. Come on. And bring in hither the poor. Wait, wait, wait. And bring in. Read that part again. Emphasize that. Go out quickly into the streets. Come on. And lanes of the city. Read. And bring in. And what? And bring in. And what? And bring in.

Do you know the honor it is to be used to bring somebody in? That's what I want to be used for. To be used to bring somebody in. You understand? Our job is to bring people in. Get James chapter 5. You being used. You sisters being used. Because guess what? When you hand a flyer, that flyer could change their life, because you bringing them in. That's what we want to be used for, to save lives. Read James 5. What verse do I want? He that converteth the sinner. 20. Come on.

note.label: Final Call: Message to the Black Man

points: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple: you cannot be Christ's disciple if you are not willing to carry your cross, your burdens, and follow after him.

So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple. This is the point of hating mother and father: if you are not willing to forsake all you have, to make sacrifices, including your own life, you cannot be Christ's disciple. You have to be willing to die for what you believe in.

Which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? You had better sit down and count the cost. People will mock you if you start in this truth and give up: brothers and sisters, you talk all that good talk to your family, and then you go back; they are going to laugh at you. This man began to build, and was not able to finish.

If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children: the hate here means you're not trimming your ways against what the Lord said to benefit them. These are persons closest to you, knit to your soul. But if you don't deliver that child up so he can be corrected, because you tried the Bible and it's not working, you're enabling the behavior, and eventually it will pull you out of the truth.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

points: After the video of the apology: once you open your mouth and declare yourself to keep this gospel and teach this understanding, you cannot go back. If any man come to me and hate not his father, mother, wife, children, brethren and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. If you are still tied to family and friends who dishonor the Most High to his face continually, and you want to walk hand in hand with them, the Lord cannot use you. Whosoever doth not bear his cross cannot be my disciple.

Video played: the woke cousin who pulls up to the Fourth of July cookout. A week ago he posted all that Israelite stuff, do not invite me to any Fourth of July or Juneteenth events, do not celebrate birthdays or Easter; now he is at the cookout saying you cannot take Facebook seriously, and eating the pork he called the devil's beef. Captain: this is how you look when you go back on the word of the Lord. Now you are in blasphemy, denying Christ.

When we first started listening to the bishop's classes, we used to ride through the neighborhood with the windows down blasting the class. That joy you once had, you have to renew over and over; you will hit a plateau and have to keep fighting through it. It will come as correction; now you have people saying camp 101 is boring, sitting all day on the Sabbath is boring. This is what we signed up for, because what is lined up for the children of light our minds cannot fathom. Stay on your A game; the gospel is our profession.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? He did not count the cost. The same with the entertainer who was shamed on air for endorsing what was done to a child, and you could see his posture drop. He declared, I am an Israelite, the twelve tribes, and then had to say sorry and hold the hand of the one he had exposed. He was not even talking like himself in that clip.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation and is not able to finish, all that behold it begin to mock him: this man began to build and was not able to finish. Some of you take this as a fad and do not count the cost: I am an Israelite this season and next season you are gone; I used to wear those; one time I was an Israelite, I was a Muslim. You played with it. You will be mocked; the Lord purposely sets that spirit so you are exposed: you professed to be a servant of God, and now look at you cutting the cake at the cookout, after all the commanding and hating you did. Shame. Actions shall be weighed.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Or what king, going to make war, sitteth not down first and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh with twenty thousand? Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage and desireth conditions of peace: he waves the white flag because he did not estimate the overpowering; he was dismayed. That is why the Lord constantly reminds you: be not dismayed by them; do the work; stay focused on the mission, or you will be confounded by the wicked. Stay on the job, harden your face and your spirit constantly.
